subject: African Lion
fact: Lions are the only cats that regularly live in social groups called prides.

subject: African Elephant
fact: African elephants are the largest living land animals.

subject: Giraffe
fact: Giraffes use their long necks to reach leaves high in trees.

subject: Plains Zebra
fact: Each zebra has a unique pattern of stripes.

subject: Cheetah
fact: Cheetahs are the fastest land animals over short distances.

subject: Leopard
fact: Leopards are strong climbers and often rest in trees.

subject: White Rhinoceros
fact: White rhinos have wide square lips that help them graze on grass.

subject: Black Rhinoceros
fact: Black rhinos use pointed upper lips to grasp leaves and twigs.

subject: Hippopotamus
fact: Hippos spend much of the day in water to stay cool.

subject: African Buffalo
fact: African buffalo often travel in large herds for protection.

subject: Blue Wildebeest
fact: Wildebeest can travel long distances while following seasonal rains.

subject: Thomson's Gazelle
fact: Thomson's gazelles are quick runners that live on open grasslands.

subject: Grant's Gazelle
fact: Grant's gazelles can go for long periods without drinking free-standing water.

subject: Impala
fact: Impalas can leap high and far to escape danger.

subject: Greater Kudu
fact: Greater kudus have large ears and males grow spiral horns.

subject: Eland
fact: Elands are the largest living antelopes.

subject: Gemsbok
fact: Gemsbok have long straight horns and are well adapted to dry habitats.

subject: Sable Antelope
fact: Sable antelopes have curved horns and strong necks.

subject: Waterbuck
fact: Waterbucks are often found near rivers and lakes.

subject: Springbok
fact: Springboks can make high stiff-legged jumps called pronking.

subject: Common Warthog
fact: Warthogs often kneel on their front legs while grazing.

subject: African Wild Dog
fact: African wild dogs live in close-knit packs and hunt cooperatively.

subject: Spotted Hyena
fact: Spotted hyenas have powerful jaws and live in groups called clans.

subject: Striped Hyena
fact: Striped hyenas are mostly active at night.

subject: Jackal
fact: Jackals are adaptable canids that eat many different kinds of food.

subject: Meerkat
fact: Meerkats take turns watching for danger while others forage.

subject: Mongoose
fact: Mongooses are quick predators that eat insects and other small animals.

subject: Aardvark
fact: Aardvarks use strong claws to dig for ants and termites.

subject: Porcupine
fact: Porcupines protect themselves with sharp quills.

subject: Baboon
fact: Baboons live in social groups and communicate with many sounds and gestures.

subject: Vervet Monkey
fact: Vervet monkeys use different alarm calls for different predators.

subject: Colobus Monkey
fact: Colobus monkeys spend much of their time in trees and eat many leaves.

subject: Ostrich
fact: Ostriches are the largest living birds and can run very fast.

subject: Secretary Bird
fact: Secretary birds hunt snakes and other small animals on the ground.

subject: Crowned Crane
fact: Crowned cranes have a distinctive crown of golden feathers.

subject: Marabou Stork
fact: Marabou storks have huge wings and often soar on warm air currents.

subject: African Fish Eagle
fact: African fish eagles catch fish with powerful talons.

subject: Helmeted Guineafowl
fact: Helmeted guineafowl travel in flocks and make loud calls.

subject: Shoebill
fact: Shoebills have enormous shoe-shaped bills for catching fish.

subject: Flamingo
fact: Flamingos get pink coloring from pigments in the food they eat.

subject: Nile Crocodile
fact: Nile crocodiles are powerful swimmers that spend much of their lives near water.

subject: African Rock Python
fact: African rock pythons kill prey by constriction rather than venom.

subject: Black Mamba
fact: Black mambas are fast snakes that usually try to avoid people.

subject: Puff Adder
fact: Puff adders rely on camouflage and often remain still when threatened.

subject: African Spurred Tortoise
fact: African spurred tortoises dig burrows to escape extreme heat.

subject: Nile Monitor
fact: Nile monitors are large lizards that can swim well.

subject: Chameleon
fact: Chameleons can move their eyes independently and shoot out long sticky tongues.

subject: Agama Lizard
fact: Many male agamas develop bright colors during breeding season.

subject: Dung Beetle
fact: Dung beetles help recycle nutrients by burying animal droppings.

subject: Termite
fact: Termites build large colonies and help break down dead plant material.

subject: Tsetse Fly
fact: Tsetse flies are found in parts of sub-Saharan Africa and feed on blood.

subject: Acacia Ant
fact: Some ants live in acacia trees and help defend the trees from herbivores.

subject: Honey Badger
fact: Honey badgers are strong diggers and are known for bold behavior.

subject: Bat-Eared Fox
fact: Bat-eared foxes use their huge ears to locate insects underground.

subject: Serval
fact: Servals have long legs and large ears that help them hunt in tall grass.

subject: Caracal
fact: Caracals can leap high into the air to catch birds.

subject: Genet
fact: Genets are agile nocturnal mammals with long tails.

subject: Okapi
fact: Okapis are relatives of giraffes and have striped legs.

subject: Greater Flamingo
fact: Greater flamingos use special bills to filter tiny food from water.

subject: Pangolin
fact: Pangolins are mammals covered in protective keratin scales.
